summary.text: Take \(n=8=2^3\), so \(\Omega(8)=3\) is odd and at least \(3\). In the Möbius sum only the \(d=4,8\) terms survive, giving \(a(8)=8!(H_8-H_4)=25584>0\), contradicting the predicted negativity.

full_proof.text:
Let
\[
H_n=\sum_{j=1}^n\frac1j
\]
denote the \(n\)-th harmonic number. The sequence \(a(n)\) is characterized by
\[
\sum_{k\mid n}\frac{a(k)}{k!}=H_n.
\]
Set \(b(k)=a(k)/k!\). Then the defining relation is
\[
\sum_{k\mid n}b(k)=H_n.
\]
By Möbius inversion,
\[
b(n)=\sum_{d\mid n}\mu(n/d)H_d,
\]
where \(\mu\) is the Möbius function. Consequently,
\[
a(n)=n!\sum_{d\mid n}\mu(n/d)H_d.
\]

We disprove the proposed equivalence by taking \(n=8\).

The positive divisors of \(8\) are
\[
1,2,4,8.
\]
Thus the Möbius-inversion formula gives
\[
\frac{a(8)}{8!}
 =\mu(8)H_1+\mu(4)H_2+\mu(2)H_4+\mu(1)H_8.
\]
The relevant Möbius values are
\[
\mu(8)=0,\qquad \mu(4)=0,\qquad \mu(2)=-1,\qquad \mu(1)=1.
\]
Indeed, \(8\) and \(4\) are divisible by the square \(2^2\), so their Möbius values vanish; \(2\) is a product of one distinct prime, so \(\mu(2)=-1\); and by definition \(\mu(1)=1\). Therefore
\[
\frac{a(8)}{8!}=H_8-H_4.
\]
The terms through \(1/4\) cancel in this difference, leaving
\[
H_8-H_4=\frac15+\frac16+\frac17+\frac18.
\]
Using the common denominator \(840\), this is
\[
\frac{168+140+120+105}{840}=\frac{533}{840}.
\]
Since
\[
8!=40320=48\cdot 840,
\]
we obtain
\[
a(8)=40320\cdot\frac{533}{840}=48\cdot533=25584.
\]
In particular,
\[
a(8)>0,
\]
so the assertion \(a(8)<0\) is false.

On the other hand,
\[
8=2^3.
\]
Hence the total number of prime factors of \(8\), counted with multiplicity, is
\[
\Omega(8)=3.
\]
This number is odd, and it is at least \(3\). Thus the condition
\[
\Omega(8)\text{ is odd and }\Omega(8)\ge 3
\]
is true, while \(a(8)<0\) is false.

Therefore, at the positive integer \(n=8\), the two sides of the proposed equivalence have different truth values. It is consequently false that for every positive integer \(n\),
\[
a(n)<0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \Omega(n)\text{ is odd and at least }3.
\]
